concepts.title: Dialogue Archive
concepts.brief:
APPLICATION: DIALOGUE ARCHIVE, a Morbotron-like searchable Star Trek episode dialogue and frame browser. A genuinely useful media research tool, shown in its search results and selected-frame state.
Composition: dominant upper-left warm peach elbow flows into a top segmented search rail. Left segmented vertical navigation labels SEARCH, EPISODES, SAVED, EXPORT; SEARCH selected. Top-right title DIALOGUE ARCHIVE. Large searchable field on black with lavender underline contains "coffee"; a peach SEARCH end segment. A filter strip reads VOYAGER / ALL SEASONS / DIALOGUE. Middle left has four compact horizontal results with small rectangular episode still thumbnails, episode name, timecode and one short dialogue excerpt; first is selected in a peach band. Right half is a large rectangular selected still: a tasteful cinematic Star Trek Voyager bridge scene with Captain Janeway, not a glowing illustration. Beneath the still: "THE CLOUD", "01:06 / 12:41", and the exact short quotation "There's coffee in that nebula." Below that a segmented timeline with highlighted current position and native-looking LCARS action segments PREVIOUS, PLAY, NEXT, SAVE FRAME. A lower lavender elbow encloses a short transcript with three speaker-labelled rows and the current line highlighted. Search and media controls must be legible and the largest photo must not swallow the LCARS structure. Frame still content is illustrative.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high fidelity application UI concept as a flat, straight-on, edge-to-edge landscape screen, approximately 3:2. Transform the attached approved TNG LCARS visual studies into a different working application described below. Image 1 is the elbow and typography reference; image 2 is the overall screen composition reference. Preserve their graphic discipline and natural ultracondensed letterforms. This is an application screenshot concept, no device mockup, no perspective, no desk, no outer marketing board.
Visual direction: authentic late-1980s/1990s Star Trek The Next Generation LCARS. Pure black background, opaque flat warm peach #FCC19F, lavender #BAA4E5, mauve #C082A9, occasional amber #EB943A. Large carefully constructed elbows where a broad vertical spine turns into a thinner horizontal rail. Outer and inner corners are tangent circular arcs with DIFFERENT independent radii, the inner black counter has a crisp curved cutout. Broad arm to thin rail ratio around 4:1; outer radius roughly 72 and inner radius 48 at a 144pt spine. Consistent narrow black gutters separating segments. Straight square segment joins; rounded capsule ends only at exposed rail endpoints. Composition-specific connected rails organize actual content.
Typography: extremely narrow tall upright uppercase LCARS GTJ3 / Helvetica Ultra Compressed visual character as shown in reference, natural glyphs, small right-aligned black labels within colored rail segments, peach or lavender type on black. Large narrow section titles. Body prose may use a modest readable sans serif. Dense but carefully structured information, calibrated black negative space, numeric micro-labels only at useful structural junctions. Native-app usability: visible selected state, readable labels, stable navigation and purposeful content.
Avoid generic dashboard cards, uniform rounded rectangles, modern SaaS styling, neon cyan cyberpunk, gradients, glass, glow, bevels, shadows, 3D controls, thick outlines everywhere, oversized generic sans serif headings, excessive filler text. Make the elbow silhouette and font the defining elements. No claim of official licensing, no watermark.

concepts.title: Reference Library
concepts.brief:
APPLICATION: REFERENCE LIBRARY, a Memory Beta-style Star Trek encyclopedia reader with search, article hierarchy, sources and cross references. Shown on a ship-class article, with a clear EXPANDED UNIVERSE label so content provenance is visible.
Composition distinctly different from the media app: slim lavender upper rule leads into a tall warm peach left navigation elbow, large section heading LIBRARY COMPUTER ACCESS at upper right. Left spine navigation SEARCH, STARSHIPS, PEOPLE, PLACES, BOOKMARKS, with STARSHIPS selected. Main two-thirds is a readable article titled "GALAXY CLASS", with a short lead paragraph in readable small sans serif, small LCARS section tabs OVERVIEW / SERVICE HISTORY / TECHNICAL / SOURCES, and three concise text sections broken by thin peach rules. A clean flat orthographic side-view line schematic of a Galaxy-class starship is placed inside the article, lavender and peach lines on black. The narrow right region is an integrated connected-rail reference panel, no rounded card, with labelled fields TYPE / EXPLORER, OPERATOR / STARFLEET, KNOWN VESSELS / ENTERPRISE-D and linked entries. Below the article a lavender bottom elbow organizes related records and a citation list. Include a breadcrumb "STARSHIPS / FEDERATION / GALAXY CLASS", a small search field, SAVE and OPEN SOURCE actions. This must look like a comfortable usable reference reading interface that happens to follow canonical TNG graphic language. Body paragraphs should be short and coherent, not fake gibberish.

concepts.title: Stellar Atlas
concepts.brief:
APPLICATION: STELLAR ATLAS, a practical amateur astronomy app for searching real celestial objects and planning observations. Selected target M42 / ORION NEBULA. Use a real observing workflow rather than fictional spacecraft gauges.
Composition: asymmetric large cartographic workspace across middle-left, framed by a warm peach upper-left elbow and a lower lavender secondary elbow for tonight's observing list. Top-right title STELLAR ATLAS. Left rail navigation SKY MAP, TARGETS, SESSION, LOG, with SKY MAP selected. Main map is a BLACK scientific star chart with tiny white/lavender stars, a sparse coordinate grid, thin constellation connector lines, Orion named, an obvious peach crosshair on M42, and a small labelled target callout; NOT a photographic galaxy wallpaper, NOT an orbit diagram. The right instrument column has M42 / ORION NEBULA, concise fields TYPE / EMISSION NEBULA, CONSTELLATION / ORION, MAGNITUDE / 4.0, then a restrained altitude-versus-time curve with labelled axes and a highlighted observing window. Clearly label projected values as SESSION PREVIEW. Bottom connected rail contains observing-list rows M42, M45, M31 with a peach selected row and action segments ADD TO SESSION, CENTER TARGET, LOG OBSERVATION. Keep fine scientific marks subordinate to bold authentic LCARS rail geometry. Make this a plausible macOS or iPadOS astronomy application.

concepts.title: Engineering
concepts.brief:
APPLICATION: ENGINEERING, a practical macOS system monitor using TNG engineering-console visual grammar. Real data domains: CPU, GPU, memory, storage, network; avoid fictional warp-core metrics. Values are mock data.
Composition: a wide engineering status console built from nested warm peach and lavender connected elbow rails, different from the encyclopedia and star map. Large top-right heading ENGINEERING / LOCAL SYSTEM. Left segmented spine labels OVERVIEW, PROCESSES, STORAGE, NETWORK, with OVERVIEW selected. Dominant center is a flat orthographic computer subsystem bus schematic, thin peach and lavender lines connecting rectangular CPU, GPU, MEMORY, SSD and NETWORK modules; small vertical segmented utilization bars embedded alongside modules and readable numeric readouts. Right column contains two dense small line graphs CPU HISTORY / 60 SEC and NETWORK / 60 SEC, with axes and clear labels. A lower lavender elbow and horizontal rail organize a real process table with columns PROCESS, CPU, MEMORY and rows WindowServer, Safari, Xcode, LCARSCatalog. Footer includes UPDATE INTERVAL / 1 SEC, PAUSE, EXPORT SNAPSHOT. Distinctively TNG task-specific engineering information design, not five identical metric cards. Use structured number banks and discrete indicator strips as supporting micrographics, clearly separate from the actual numeric readings.
